title: Workspace Lambda Execution Policy and Model Workload Governance v1
goal: Design, implement, and adversarially validate a fail-closed workload admission, trusted model/dependency cache, resource-governance, and execution-evidence layer on top of the accepted Lambda P5 CPU and gpu-small autonomous runner substrate so ChatGPT/GitHub-driven work can safely execute pinned model-scale workloads without granting candidate workflow code the ability to invent capabilities, persist mutable cross-job state, access production/scientific state, or widen host authority.
acceptance_criteria: The accepted parent substrate remains the immutable starting boundary: one-job JIT runners, separate CPU and gpu-small scale sets, unprivileged GitHub-facing controller, credential-blind root provisioner, project UID isolation, private/local-network denial, production-state denial, and residue-free cleanup.

A versioned declarative workload-admission contract exists and binds repository/project, trusted workflow identity, exact candidate SHA, workload class, execution profile, model/dependency identities, resource class, egress class, secrets class, filesystem/state-effect class, cache class, and required evidence.

Workflow/candidate input is treated as a claim to validate against root-owned policy; candidate code cannot directly widen device, filesystem, network, secret, cache-promotion, production-state, or runtime authority.

Approved workload classes distinguish ordinary cpu-test, hardware-only gpu-small, model acquisition, trusted cache promotion, offline model evaluation, and later gpu-heavy/dual-GPU work; production daemon/scientific-state mutation remains outside ordinary CI.

Model acquisition is separated from model evaluation. Candidate model-eval jobs receive no model-registry credential and run from promoted read-only content with offline/local-files-only behavior by default.
Trusted model/dependency cache promotion is performed by a separate trusted authority unavailable to candidate workflow code.

A promoted model object records exact upstream repository, exact immutable revision/commit, source/archive and per-file digests, resulting tree/content digest, license/usage metadata, serialization format, custom-code/executable-dependency risk, promotion recipe identity, and a durable promotion receipt.
Mutable branch names such as main are never the durable identity of a promoted model/runtime object; resolve-once inputs are converted to exact immutable revisions before promotion.

Unsafe serialization is fail-closed by default: safetensors/safe serialization is preferred, pickle/deserialization paths that can execute arbitrary code require an explicit separately reviewed exception, and remote/custom model code is treated as executable dependency material.
Dependency/runtime identity is pinned independently of model weights and is included in admission and execution receipts.
Trusted cache is read-only to candidate jobs; candidate jobs write only per-job workspace or ephemeral staging and cannot mutate another job's promoted cache object.
Cache completeness can be verified offline; partial/incomplete snapshots fail closed rather than being treated as valid local models.

Resource policy covers CPU, RAM, GPU UUIDs, wall-clock timeout, TasksMax/process count, scratch/staging disk ceilings, concurrency, OOM/timeout/disk-pressure behavior, process cleanup, GPU-process cleanup, and model-server leak detection.

Network policy is explicit by workload class. Model-eval is offline/no-model-egress by default; acquisition/promotion gets only the minimum registry/public egress required and still cannot reach local/private/production services.

Secrets policy is explicit by workload class. Candidate model-eval jobs receive no personal, controller, SSH, production database, or model-registry credentials; any trusted acquisition credential is isolated from candidate code.

Every admitted job produces a non-secret receipt that binds policy/admission identity, workflow SHA, candidate SHA, execution profile, model/runtime/cache object identity, GPU UUID(s), relevant CUDA/runtime versions, resource evidence, terminal status, and cleanup result.

The controller/provisioner rejects unknown workload classes, mismatched project/profile/model bindings, stale/replayed admissions, unauthorized gpu-heavy requests, and attempts to bypass cache/promotion policy.

Controller restart/recovery, duplicate/replayed request IDs, cleanup failure, kill-switch operation, timeout, CPU/GPU process leak, CUDA OOM, RAM OOM or equivalent bounded memory failure, disk-pressure failure, and concurrent CPU/GPU demand are tested fail-closed.
The existing trusted-cache policy is promoted from static design into executable policy/tooling without silently changing project scientific authority.

The first model-scale pilot uses the already-certified Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B exact revision 851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a and does not introduce a new heavyweight model before the policy/cache path is proven.

The first model pilot uses a non-scientific bounded canary/benchmark, runs on the accepted single-A4500 class, performs no production routing change or scientific materialization, leaves no resident model server/processes, and proves cleanup before any research-engine scientific benchmark uses the lane.
gpu-heavy/dual-GPU remains denied until a separate policy decision and acceptance gate after single-GPU model-eval plus adversarial/cache/resource validation pass.
Current GitHub-hosted CI remains a known-good control path and is not replaced by heavyweight Lambda validation.
The task preserves project ownership: workspace-control owns cross-project admission/cache/execution policy; research-engine owns model-specific scientific/runtime truth and benchmark semantics.

Every substantial ChatGPT response for this task follows the current Heartbeat v2 contract: call heartbeat_begin_turn exactly once as the first Heartbeat operation in that assistant response; reuse its returned opaque turn_id for every later heartbeat_update in that same response; never call heartbeat_begin_turn a second time before sending the assistant response; heartbeat_open is retired.
constraints: Do not weaken or bypass the accepted P5 CPU or gpu-small isolation boundaries merely to simplify model execution.
Do not enable gpu-heavy, dual-GPU, sustained model servers, production daemon execution, or scientific-state mutation before their explicit policy/acceptance gates.
Do not grant candidate code root, sudo, Docker-socket access, personal home access, controller credentials, SSH keys, browser credentials, or production database credentials.
Do not let candidate workflow code invoke trusted-cache promotion directly.
Do not use model repository branch names or tags as final promoted identity when an exact commit/revision can be resolved.
Do not permit arbitrary pickle loading or trust_remote_code/custom model code by default; executable model material requires explicit pinning/review and a separately declared exception.
Do not store model registry tokens, GitHub credentials, JIT config, SSH keys, environment files with secrets, or production credentials in trusted model/package caches.
Do not make candidate-writable caches persistent across jobs.
Do not silently reuse a cached model/runtime object whose recorded digest, exact revision, dependency identity, license/risk metadata, or completeness check no longer matches policy.
Do not let model-eval jobs fetch missing model files from the network; missing/incomplete promoted content must fail closed.
Do not allow model acquisition/promotion to execute model inference merely because artifacts were downloaded.
Do not mutate research-engine production routing as part of policy-layer acceptance.
Do not duplicate research-engine scientific/model-selection truth in workspace-control; reference exact owning contracts and identities.
Do not expand to another repository/project UID until this task has accepted its admission/cache/recovery semantics on research-engine.
Keep operator-facing temporary diagnostic/benchmark artifacts under ~/adamArchives/Adam/workspace-control-tmp/ or an explicit visible WORKSPACE_CONTROL_TMP_ROOT.

Operator-facing shell instructions must preserve the interactive SSH/session on every validation or install failure. Never emit a top-level `exit`, `logout`, `exec`, shell-kill, or equivalent in a pasteable operator block. Put fail-fast checks inside an explicit child shell/subshell or otherwise return control to the operator prompt.

Any operator command that depends on a repository must enter that repository inside the same child shell/subshell, verify the exact git toplevel/cleanliness/HEAD before privileged execution, and print diagnostics on mismatch without terminating the parent SSH session.

Follow the current Heartbeat v2 plugin contract for every substantial assistant response: call heartbeat_begin_turn exactly once as the first Heartbeat operation; preserve its returned opaque turn_id for every later heartbeat_update until the response is sent; do not call heartbeat_begin_turn again merely because the work shifts phases within the same response; never use the removed heartbeat_open operation; use heartbeat_get only for explicit history/recovery inspection. The plugin's own current tool/schema contract supersedes older Heartbeat wording.
